answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids, with larger stakes required for more influence. A protocol randomly assigns bonded agents to verify one another’s work, then slashes stake when independent evidence confirms fraud. Creating sybils no longer gives free votes: each identity ties up capital, and coordinated false claims risk losing it. The karst survey may wander into an opal-rich region, but duplicating agents to capture its reward means duplicating the costly bonds too.
